newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures higher in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures higher in listless trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were higher Wednesday, recovering Tuesday's losses in listless trade that was characterized by little news, industry sources said.
"We're trading just a little bit higher, but there is absolutely nothing going on," said one Houston based futures trader.

As of 1250 EDT, July Palo Verde (PV) was up 21 cents at $26.70 following exchanges in a range of $26.65-27.10, while August was up 10 cents at the day's low of $28.90 after trade as high as $29.15 per megawatt hour (MWh).

July California Oregon Border (COB) was up 46 cents at $17.15 after trades in a range of $17.00-17.40, while August was up 15 cents at the day's low of $20.70 following trade as high as $20.80 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1210 EDT an estimated total of 282 COB and 236 PV contracts had traded.
Trade remained within a recent range on the lack of news, the sources said.

In Western generation, a 450 megawatt (MW) unit at the San Juan coal-fired plant in New Mexico was expected to restart Thursday, and a 670 MW unit at the Centralia coal-fired station in Washington was scheduled to return to service this weekend.
Forecasters called temperatures in the Northwest to run near to above normal next week with bouts of unsettled weather conditions.
Fair and warm weather was expected to stay in the Southwest with readings averaging three to six degrees Fahrenheit above normal through the middle of next week.

Separately, industry sources told Reuters Wednesday that a a Western Systems Coordinating Council committee is proposing a summertime rating for the Pacific Intertie of 6,900 MW, down from the current springtime limit of 7,200 MW.
As of 1250 EDT, NYMEX July Henry Hub natural gas was trading up 1.6 cents at $2.087 per million British thermal units.
COB open interest for June 11 rose five to 6,671, while PV open interest rose 239 to 7,122, NYMEX said.
